controls.controlDescription: Establish clear and specific procedures to control physical access to facilities, servers, and devices containing ePHI to prevent unauthorized access or theft.
Ensure workstations accessing ePHI are positioned and protected to prevent unauthorized viewing or access by patients or visitors.
Designate a security official and implement a documented security management process, including risk management and sanctions.
Implement policies governing the use, access, and protection of mobile devices containing or accessing ePHI.
Maintain an updated asset log for all hardware devices that store or transmit ePHI, including historical and current devices.
Conduct a formal HIPAA risk assessment annually to identify vulnerabilities and risks to ePHI.
Conduct and document ongoing HIPAA training and awareness programs for all employees.
Designate a HIPAA Compliance Officer responsible for implementing and enforcing HIPAA policies and risk management practices.
Develop policies and procedures to maintain the integrity and accuracy of ePHI within the organization.
Ensure signed Business Associate Agreements are executed with all vendors handling ePHI.
Restrict access to ePHI based on job responsibilities and ensure only minimum necessary information is accessible.
Establish procedures for reporting and escalating potential security incidents to the HIPAA Compliance Officer.
Assign unique usernames or identification codes to each individual accessing ePHI systems.
Define procedures for releasing or disclosing ePHI to patients, business associates, and during emergencies.
Implement controls to monitor and track changes or alterations made to ePHI.
Encrypt ePHI during storage and transmission, especially when transmitted outside the organization.
Maintain logs of all access activities related to ePHI systems and records.
Document and enforce secure login and logout procedures for all staff accessing ePHI.
Implement measures to reduce identified risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
Regularly review audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
Authorize and supervise workforce members based on job duties and access needs.
Verify workforce clearance before granting access to ePHI.
Establish formal procedures to grant, modify, and remove access to ePHI.
Define containment, investigation, remediation, and post-incident review steps for security incidents.
Perform periodic technical and nontechnical evaluations after environmental or operational changes.
Establish procedures to obtain necessary ePHI during an emergency.
Define acceptable workstation use rules for devices that access ePHI.
Maintain facility security, access validation, contingency operations, and maintenance records for sites housing ePHI.
Ensure reusable media are sanitized before re-use and track media accountability.
Perform a risk analysis to determine whether encryption of ePHI is appropriate and required within the organization.
Implement alternative security measures when encryption is determined not to be appropriate to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI.
Implement controls to prevent unauthorized access to ePHI during electronic transmission.
Maintain audit logs tracking login attempts to systems containing ePHI for monitoring and auditing purposes.
Review ePHI access logs regularly to identify and investigate unauthorized access attempts or suspicious activity.

controls.controlPoint: Protection Against Unauthorized Alteration or Destruction
controls.controlDescription: Implement controls to ensure ePHI is not altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
Implement identity management and access control mechanisms to regulate user access to ePHI systems.
Restrict access to ePHI only to authorized users who require access to perform job responsibilities.
Implement mechanisms to authenticate ePHI and verify that it has not been altered or destroyed without authorization.
Implement encryption mechanisms to protect ePHI when transmitted electronically.
Designate a privacy official and a complaint contact person/office, and maintain a complaint/non-retaliation process.
Verify the identity and authority of any person requesting PHI before disclosure.
Add procedures for the individual rights to request restrictions, receive confidential communications, amend PHI, and obtain an accounting of disclosures.
Ensure the Notice of Privacy Practices includes all required content, an effective date, and prompt revision/distribution after material changes.

Add authorization controls for special/non-routine disclosures, including valid authorization criteria, revocation handling, psychotherapy notes, sale of PHI, and other authorization-based disclosures.
Add mitigation procedures for harmful effects caused by impermissible uses or disclosures.
Add reproductive-health PHI restrictions and attestation controls required by the 2024 final rule.
Provide appropriate internal training to employees regarding permissible and impermissible uses and disclosures of PHI.
Ensure written patient authorization is obtained before PHI is used or disclosed for marketing, fundraising, or research purposes.
Maintain procedures to provide patients access to their ePHI within 30 days or earlier if required by applicable state laws.
Establish policies and procedures to notify OCR/HHS promptly and issue media notifications for breaches affecting more than 500 individuals.
Establish processes for notifying affected individuals within required timelines after a confirmed breach.
Establish policies and procedures to report breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals to the OCR website as required.
Maintain documented policies and procedures addressing HIPAA Privacy, Security, and Breach Notification Rule requirements.
Ensure all employees read, acknowledge, and legally attest to HIPAA-related policies and procedures.
Maintain documentation evidencing employee legal attestation to HIPAA policies and procedures.
Conduct and document annual reviews and updates of HIPAA policies and procedures.
Require employees to sign confidentiality agreements protecting PHI and ePHI.
Prohibit employees from removing paper or electronic PHI from organizational premises without authorization.
Establish procedures for the secure disposal of physical PHI and electronic PHI.

controls.subDomain: Media & Disposal Controls – Physical Records Protection
controls.controlDescription: Implement procedures to render physical PHI unreadable and incapable of reconstruction prior to disposal.

controls.subDomain: Media & Disposal Controls – Electronic Media Sanitization
controls.controlDescription: Implement procedures to securely erase ePHI from electronic devices when no longer needed.

controls.controlPoint: Secure Storage of PHI/ePHI Before Disposal
controls.controlDescription: Securely store physical PHI and devices containing ePHI until proper disposal is completed.
Maintain and enforce sanction policies for employees who violate HIPAA requirements or organizational policies.
Establish procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords used to access systems containing ePHI.
Implement procedures to periodically review and validate employee access to ePHI systems.

controls.controlPoint: Termination and Role Change Access Removal
controls.controlDescription: Establish procedures to terminate or modify ePHI access when employees leave or change job roles.
Implement procedures to recover all organizational devices containing ePHI when employees leave the organization.
Establish and maintain a documented contingency plan to address emergencies and disruptions affecting ePHI.
Develop written policies and procedures for responding to emergency situations involving systems containing ePHI.
Ensure all ePHI is backed up regularly and exact copies are available for disaster recovery and restoration purposes.
Maintain written procedures to sustain critical business operations and access to ePHI during emergencies.
Identify critical applications and data to prioritize recovery during disruptions.

controls.subDomain: Administrative Safeguards – Contingency Plan Testing & Revision
controls.controlDescription: Regularly test, review, and update contingency plans to ensure effectiveness and alignment with organizational changes.
Designate Privacy/Security Officer(s) responsible for HIPAA compliance.
Retain HIPAA-required policies, procedures, and records for at least 6 years.
